---
title: "Mapping place mentions"
subtitle: "Examine state-name matches before drawing them"
description: "Learn why place-name matches require checks before mapping. Keep non-place meanings visible in check records."
categories: [information visualization, maps, place names]
---

`Washington` is the first problem in this map. In presidential speeches it can
mean a person, a city, the federal government, or the state. The author must find
which readings are present.

Ben still wants a map from the speeches, but the name match is only the first
step.

Mapping **locations** requires more than finding a name. The reader must find
whether the name refers to a place. If so, the reader must find which place it names.
The counting unit and the basemap's coverage also require explicit decisions.

This lesson uses U.S. inaugural-address paragraphs and the state names bundled
with R. The check rules and labels below are the author's judgement after
reading the matches in this corpus. They are not an independent geoparser, a
system that finds and resolves place names.

::: {.callout-tip}
## What you will learn

This lesson shows how to:

- match U.S. state names with case-sensitive, whole-word rules
- compare naive matches with examined readings
- exclude person, river, event, government, and pre-statehood readings from the map
- count speeches with at least one examined state reading
- draw symbols with area scaling instead of a choropleth
- state a basemap's coverage and projection limits.
:::

## Match state names before examining them

The source data is the shared inaugural-address paragraph table used in earlier
lessons. Every match retains a paragraph ID and speech ID. The matcher sorts
state names from longest to shortest. It therefore selects `West Virginia`
before `Virginia` when those matches overlap.

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel)
library(purrr)
library(stringr)
library(tibble)
library(tidyr)

source("R/inaugural-corpus.R")
source("R/lesson-figures.R")

paragraphs <- inaugural_paragraphs()

state_lookup <- tibble(state = datasets::state.name) |>
  arrange(desc(str_length(state)), state)

empty_matches <- function() {
  tibble(
    state = character(),
    start = integer(),
    end = integer(),
    mention = character()
  )
}

state_pattern <- function(state_name) {
  regex(
    paste0("\\b", str_replace_all(state_name, " ", "\\\\s+"), "\\b"),
    ignore_case = FALSE
  )
}

find_all_state_candidates <- function(text) {
  state_lookup$state |>
    map_dfr(\(state_name) {
      locations <- str_locate_all(text, state_pattern(state_name))[[1]]
      if (nrow(locations) == 0L) {
        return(empty_matches())
      }

      tibble(
        state = state_name,
        start = as.integer(locations[, 1]),
        end = as.integer(locations[, 2]),
        mention = str_sub(text, start, end)
      )
    }) |>
    arrange(start, desc(end - start), state)
}

choose_longest_nonoverlap <- function(candidates, text_length) {
  if (nrow(candidates) == 0L) {
    return(candidates)
  }

  kept <- rep(FALSE, nrow(candidates))
  used_positions <- rep(FALSE, text_length)

  for (row_number in seq_len(nrow(candidates))) {
    span <- candidates$start[row_number]:candidates$end[row_number]
    if (!any(used_positions[span])) {
      kept[row_number] <- TRUE
      used_positions[span] <- TRUE
    }
  }

  candidates[kept, ]
}

find_state_matches <- function(text) {
  find_all_state_candidates(text) |>
    choose_longest_nonoverlap(nchar(text))
}

state_matches <- paragraphs |>
  mutate(matches = map(paragraph, find_state_matches)) |>
  filter(map_int(matches, nrow) > 0L) |>
  select(
    paragraph_id, speech_id, year, president, paragraph_words,
    paragraph, matches
  ) |>
  unnest(matches) |>
  mutate(
    match_key = str_c(paragraph_id, state, start, sep = ":"),
    context = str_squish(str_sub(
      paragraph,
      pmax(1L, start - 70L),
      pmin(nchar(paragraph), end + 70L)
    ))
  )

naive_state_counts <- state_matches |>
  summarise(
    naive_matches = n(),
    naive_speeches = n_distinct(speech_id),
    .by = state
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(naive_matches), state)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false

knitr::kable(
  naive_state_counts,
  col.names = c("Matched name", "Naive matches", "Speeches with a match"),
  caption = "Naive case-sensitive state-name matches before checks",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#| include: false

inside_longer_state <- function(text, start, end, state) {
  longer_states <- state_lookup |>
    filter(str_length(state) > str_length(.env$state)) |>
    pull(state)

  longer_states |>
    map_lgl(\(longer_state) {
      locations <- str_locate_all(text, state_pattern(longer_state))[[1]]
      if (nrow(locations) == 0L) {
        return(FALSE)
      }
      any(locations[, 1] <= start & locations[, 2] >= end)
    }) |>
    any()
}

synthetic_overlap_check <- find_state_matches(
  "West Virginia appears before Virginia in this check."
)

stopifnot(
  all(c("dplyr", "ggplot2", "ggrepel", "purrr", "stringr", "tibble", "tidyr") %in%
    loadedNamespaces()),
  !"package:maps" %in% search(),
  identical(nrow(paragraphs), 1377L),
  identical(nrow(state_matches), 67L),
  identical(n_distinct(state_matches$state), 18L),
  identical(n_distinct(state_matches$speech_id), 24L),
  identical(synthetic_overlap_check$state, c("West Virginia", "Virginia")),
  !any(pmap_lgl(
    list(
      state_matches$paragraph, state_matches$start,
      state_matches$end, state_matches$state
    ),
    inside_longer_state
  ))
)
```

The naive table counts strings. It does not distinguish `Washington` as a
person, city, or state. The next step resolves those meanings.

## Examine what each match means

The author wrote these categories after reading the 67 matches. The rules give
unresolved matches the category `uncertain` and exclude them from the map.

Each match key combines paragraph ID, matched name, and the 1-based character
start within the paragraph. This key preserves the label's sentence association
after row reordering.

```{r}

  "person", "the state name is part of a person's name or title",
  "city or federal government", "the name refers to Washington, DC, New York City, or federal power",
  "event name", "the name belongs to a named meeting or conference",
  "river", "the name refers to a river or river valley",
  "territory or republic before statehood", "the text refers to land before it became a state",
  "law or organisation name", "the name appears inside a law, congress, or organisation label",
  "state or its people", "the text refers to the state, its residents, or someone from that state",
  "uncertain", "the author could not assign a safer category after reading the context"
```

## Compare naive and examined readings

The table below keeps the naive counts beside the counts after checks. The
unit after checks is speeches with at least one state reading for a state. Repeated mentions
inside one speech do not add more weight.

```{r}
reviewed_state_counts <- review_matches |>
  filter(reviewed_state_reading) |>
  distinct(state, speech_id) |>
  count(state, name = "reviewed_state_speeches") |>
  arrange(desc(reviewed_state_speeches), state)

naive_review_comparison <- naive_state_counts |>
  left_join(reviewed_state_counts, by = join_by(state)) |>
  mutate(reviewed_state_speeches = coalesce(reviewed_state_speeches, 0L)) |>
  arrange(desc(naive_matches), state)

washington_summary <- review_matches |>
  filter(state == "Washington") |>
  summarise(
    matches = n(),
    speeches = n_distinct(speech_id),
    reviewed_state_speeches = n_distinct(speech_id[reviewed_state_reading])
  )

river_summary <- review_matches |>
  filter(state %in% c("Mississippi", "Ohio", "Missouri")) |>
  summarise(
    matches = n(),
    speeches = n_distinct(speech_id),
    categories = str_c(sort(unique(reading_category)), collapse = ", "),
    .by = state
  ) |>
  arrange(state)
```

The code finds `Washington` in 17 speeches. None of those matches means
Washington State. The code also finds `Mississippi`, `Ohio`, and `Missouri` as river
readings. Those names remain in the check tables but not on the map.

The full check table is long because every non-state reading remains visible.

## Draw the state counts after checks

The basemap comes from `ggplot2::map_data("state")`, which uses the `maps`
package state database. That database covers the 48 contiguous states and the
District of Columbia. It does not draw Alaska or Hawaii, and this lesson does
not plot their `state.center` points.

```{r}
lower48_map <- ggplot2::map_data("state")

state_centers <- tibble(
  state = datasets::state.name,
  longitude = datasets::state.center$x,
  latitude = datasets::state.center$y
) |>
  mutate(lower48_or_dc = !state %in% c("Alaska", "Hawaii"))

map_points <- reviewed_state_counts |>
  left_join(state_centers, by = join_by(state)) |>
  filter(lower48_or_dc)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false

knitr::kable(
  map_points |>
    select(state, reviewed_state_speeches, longitude, latitude) |>
    arrange(desc(reviewed_state_speeches), state),
  col.names = c(
    "State", "Speeches with examined state reading",
    "Approximate center longitude", "Approximate center latitude"
  ),
  caption = "Long description for the state-count map after checks",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#| include: false

map_alt_text <- sprintf(
  paste(
    "Lower-48 U.S. map with labelled proportional circles for seven",
    "states with examined state readings. Virginia appears in 3 speeches.",
    "North Carolina and Pennsylvania appear in 2 each. California, Iowa,",
    "Louisiana, and Nebraska appear in 1 each. A Washington State note records",
    "%d name matches in %d speeches, all with other examined meanings.",
    "Washington therefore has no circle."
  ),
  washington_summary$matches,
  washington_summary$speeches
)

stopifnot(
  identical(n_distinct(lower48_map$region), 49L),
  identical(nrow(map_points), 7L),
  !any(map_points$state %in% c("Alaska", "Hawaii")),
  identical(
    state_centers$lower48_or_dc[state_centers$state %in% c("Alaska", "Hawaii")],
    c(FALSE, FALSE)
  ),
  identical(max(map_points$reviewed_state_speeches), 3L),
  identical(sum(map_points$reviewed_state_speeches), 11L),
  str_detect(map_alt_text, fixed("22 name matches in 17 speeches")),
  !any(str_detect(state_matches$paragraph, fixed("Riverton")))
)
```

The coordinates approximate state centers. A symbol represents a count, not the
location of an event in a speech. A **choropleth** shades whole areas by value.
This map instead uses circles for small speech counts, not rates or measures
of attention. The author excludes pre-statehood references such as the
Republic of Texas from state counts.

Each circle has a state-name and count label, so the map needs no size legend.
`ggrepel` separates labels to avoid overlap. Its seed makes placement
reproducible across renders. A note explains why the map excludes Washington
from the circles.

```{r}
#| label: fig-state-reading-map
#| fig-cap: "State readings in inaugural speeches on a lower-48 basemap. Seven states remain after the author's checks."
#| fig-alt: !expr map_alt_text
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

mean_latitude <- mean(lower48_map$lat, na.rm = TRUE)
fixed_ratio <- 1 / cos(mean_latitude * pi / 180)

map_labels <- map_points |>
  mutate(
    label = str_c(state, " ", reviewed_state_speeches),
    # Circle diameter from scale_size_area(), so labels clear the circle.
    circle_size = 11 * sqrt(reviewed_state_speeches / max(reviewed_state_speeches))
  )

washington_note <- state_centers |>
  filter(state == "Washington") |>
  mutate(
    label = str_c(
      "Washington: ", washington_summary$matches, " name matches,\n",
      "none about the state"
    )
  )

ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(
    data = lower48_map,
    aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group),
    fill = "#EEF1F4",
    colour = lesson_colours[["paper"]],
    linewidth = 0.4
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = map_points,
    aes(x = longitude, y = latitude, size = reviewed_state_speeches),
    shape = 21,
    fill = lesson_colours[["accent"]],
    colour = lesson_colours[["paper"]],
    stroke = 0.8,
    alpha = 0.9
  ) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = map_labels,
    aes(x = longitude, y = latitude, label = label, point.size = circle_size),
    family = lesson_font,
    size = 3.6,
    colour = lesson_colours[["ink"]],
    seed = 8001,
    box.padding = 0.4,
    point.padding = 0.15,
    min.segment.length = 0,
    segment.colour = lesson_colours[["muted"]],
    segment.size = 0.3,
    max.overlaps = Inf
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = washington_note,
    aes(x = longitude, y = latitude, label = label),
    family = lesson_font,
    size = 3.3,
    hjust = 0,
    lineheight = 0.95,
    colour = lesson_colours[["muted"]]
  ) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 11, guide = "none") +
  coord_fixed(ratio = fixed_ratio, clip = "off") +
  labs(
    title = "After checks, only seven states remain on the map",
    subtitle = str_c(
      "Speeches with at least one examined reading of each state. ",
      "Circle area shows the count."
    ),
    caption = str_c(
      "Circles mark approximate state centres from datasets::state.center. ",
      "Alaska and Hawaii are not on this basemap."
    )
  ) +
  theme_lesson(grid = "none") +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_blank()
  )
```

```{r}
#| include: false

stopifnot(
  fixed_ratio > 1,
  fixed_ratio < 2,
  identical(nrow(map_labels), 7L),
  all(str_detect(map_labels$label, "[0-9]$")),
  identical(nrow(washington_note), 1L),
  !"Washington" %in% map_points$state,
  !any(map_points$state %in% c("Alaska", "Hawaii"))
)
```

The coordinate ratio is `1 / cos(mean latitude in radians)`, or
`r round(fixed_ratio, 2)` in this render. The plot draws one degree of latitude
about `r round(fixed_ratio, 2)` times as long as one degree of longitude. A
degree of longitude covers less distance farther from the equator.

Near the country's middle, a mile east-west and a mile north-south therefore
appear approximately equal in length. This ratio does not preserve area.
Circle areas represent speech counts. The table gives exact values.

## Relation to the earlier mapping lesson

Lesson 30 uses a **gazetteer**, a place-name reference, to obtain coordinates. This
page begins earlier. It asks whether a matched name should become a place record
at all. Names can refer to people, laws, rivers, cities, events, governments, or
places from an earlier political period.

The lower-48 map also has coverage limits. If an examined state reading referred
to Alaska or Hawaii, this page would keep it in the table and not draw it on
this basemap.

## What to remember

- A state-name match is not automatically a state reference.
- Disclose the labels developed after reading the matches.
- Count speeches, not repeated mentions, when the unit is speeches.
- Rivers, people, events, and pre-statehood references stay off the final
  map.
- `scale_size_area()` maps values to circle area. The table gives exact
  counts.
- A lower-48 basemap cannot show every U.S. state.

Ben maps seven examined states after excluding most naive matches from the
symbol layer. The table remains part of the map's explanation because it
records those exclusions.
